questions.question: **Directions: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.**
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Hygeinic** ( Given in option) - There is no such word in English or we can say that there is a spelling mistake in the word.

• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

questions.question:
**Select the option that will substitute the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no substitution is needed, select ‘No substitution required’.**

When I met the couple yesterday I noticed that the wife was __more taller__ than her husband.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e., 'taller'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• **Taller **is a **comparative **form of the adjective **tall. **
 
• We cannot use** more **before it. 
 
• Hence, **option 4** is the correct answer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• For **one syllable adjectives **

 
 
• add **-er for the comparative** and **-est for the superlative.**
 
• If the adjective has a consonant + single vowel + consonant spelling, the final consonant must be doubled before adding the ending.
 
• **Examples - **tall - taller -tallest; big - bigger -biggest
 
 
 
• For two syllables adjectives
 
 
• ​form the **comparative either by adding -er** or by **preceding the adjective with more**.
 
• These adjectives form the **superlative** either by **adding -est** or by **preceding the adjective with most.**
 
• Examples - happy - happier -happiest; tangled - more tangled - most tangled
 
 
 
• For three or more syllables adjectives
 
 
• form the **comparative by putting more** in front of the adjective, and the **superlative by putting most** in front.
 
• Examples - important - more important - most important

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

Sneha said to me, “I was watching TV.”

options.text: Sneha told me that she was watching TV.
Sneha said to me that I was watching TV.
Sneha told me that she had been watching TV.
Sneha told me that I was watching TV.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option3) i.e., 'Sneha told methat she had been watching TV.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• The given sentence is an **assertive sentence. **
 
• While changing the **narration of an assertive sentence**, we need to follow steps
 
 
• The **reporting verb said **is changed to **told. **
 
• The **conjunction 'that' **is used in place of commas and inverted commas. 
 
• The** first person 'I' **will be changed into '**she**' and the **first person** **'me'** will be **unchanged.**
 
• The **verb **(**was watching**) is in the** past continuous tense form** in the given sentence.
 
• This changes to **past perfect continuous form (had been watching) **in the indirect speech.
 
 
 
• Eventually, we will get the final sentence- " **Sneha told me that she had been watching TV.**"

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Imran has found two good jobs in the advertisements of the newspaper.

options.text: Two good jobs are being found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.
Two good jobs had found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.
Two good jobs have been found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.
Two good jobs has found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e., 'Two good jobs have been found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is an **assertive sentence**. 
 
• We need to follow these instructions while **changing the voice of an assertive sentence.**
 
 
• Find the **subject and object **of the sentence and **exchange their places**.
 
• In the given sentence the **subject is ‘Imran’**, while the **object is ‘two good jobs**’.
 
• Use **preposition by **before agent. (Imran)
 
• Always use **the third form (have been found) **of the **main verb (has found)** in passive form. 
 
• At last line up the remaining part. 
 
 
 
• Following these steps, we finally get - " **Two good jobs have been found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.**"
 
• Hence, **option 3 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.**

We don't really / want a large house; / we are looking for some comfort / and some convenience on a moderate price.

options.text: and some convenience on a moderate price
we are looking for some comfort

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e., '**and some convenience on a moderate price**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the part 'and some convenience on a moderate price'.
 
• The part is using the incorrect preposition **on**.
 
• The sentence implies that the people buying the house have a price range. 
 
• To make the sentence correct we need to use the preposition **at **which is used for an estimate (Expressing a rate) or to show something inside boundaries.
 
• Correct sentence - We don't really want a large house; we are looking for some comfort and some convenience **at** a moderate price. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The **preposition on is used **when talking

 
 
• about **time,** for specific dates and days. - She came on Sunday
 
• about **position - **in or into a position covering, touching or forming part of a surface - a picture on the wall
 
• about means of **transport - **I came on my bike.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. But a dove that happened to be sitting on a neighbouring tree saw the ant’s danger and, plucking off a leaf, let it drop into the water before him.

B. Just at that time, a fowler was spreading his net and was in the act of ensnaring the dove, when the ant, perceiving his object, bit his heel.

C. An ant went to a fountain to quench his thirst and, tumbling in, almost drowned.

D. The ant mounting upon it, was presently wafted safely ashore.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e., ‘CADB’.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly.
 
• The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 
 
• Here, only C is independent and introduces the subject of the passage which deals with an ant which almost drowned.
 
• It should be followed by **A **which moves the story forward by talking about how a dove saw the ant in danger and what action the dove took. 
 
• So, A must come after C. Then CA is the correct order.
 
• This order is only shown in option 3, which shows the full sequence as: CADB.

Thus, the correct sequence is: CADB

**C.** An ant went to a fountain to quench his thirst and, tumbling in, almost drowned.

**A.** But a dove that happened to be sitting on a neighbouring tree saw the ant’s danger and, plucking off a leaf, let it drop into the water before him.

**D. **The ant mounting upon it, was presently wafted safely ashore.

**B.** Just at that time, a fowler was spreading his net and was in the act of ensnaring the dove, when the ant, perceiving his object, bit his heel.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. However, its importance is primarily for its location.

B. But unlike other rivers, it is not used for shipping.

C. Although not the longest river, the Rio Grande is the most important river in America.

D. America has several long river systems.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e., ‘DCBA’.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly.
 
• **The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. **
 
• Here, only **C** and B are independent and introduce a topic related to the American river system. So, we look at their inter-relation. 
 
• Out of these two, only **D is truly independent while C provides more information about one of the rivers in the 'river system' introduced by D.** 
 
• So, **C** must come after **D**. Then **DC** is the **correct order.**
 
• This order is shown by both **options 2 and 4 **so, we need to look into the placements of **A **and **B.**
 
• **A **and **B **begin with **however (an adverb) **and **but (a conjunction). **
 
• **But **introduces a sentence that states an opposite viewpoint to what has been stated before. 
 
• Since **C **states that the Rio Grande is an important river, it should be followed by **B **which states that it is not used for shipping despite its importance. 
 
• So, B must come after C. Then DCB is the correct order.
 
• This order is shown in **option 2, **which shows the full sequence as:** DCBA.**

Thus, the **correct sequence is: DCBA**

**D.** America has several long river systems.

**C.** Although not the longest river, the Rio Grande is the most important river in America.

**B.** But unlike other rivers, it is not used for shipping.

**A. **However, its importance is primarily for its location.
